page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.large is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the arm64 AWS Graviton processor family. Featuring two dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers predictable single-threaded execution without hyperthreading contention. Compute resources are paired with 12.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a 32 MB L3 cache and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes 1,875 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly attached to the system, while graphics acceleration is not present.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of a dual-core ARM processor configuration. Single-core stress-ng throughput registers at an average level of 1519.59, while multi-core processing scores 3013.58, situating aggregate compute in the lower quartile. Geekbench evaluations yield a single-core score of 952.0 and a multi-core score of 1753.0. In data manipulation tests, the system achieves 2.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.34 GB/s of static web serving throughput, while memory bandwidth tests record 37.37 GB/s on large un-cached read operations and 18.32 GB/s on write operations.

The primary efficiency advantage of the is4gen.large lies in its dense local storage allocation per core. Provisioning nearly two terabytes of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity against modest two-core compute makes the platform efficient for storage-heavy architectures where large compute footprints are unnecessary. However, the modest vCPU count and low parallel throughput introduce tradeoffs, limiting efficiency for compute-heavy batch processing, intensive machine learning tasks, or large-scale code compilation.

The instance is best matched with entry-level database workloads, distributed data nodes, stream processing buffers, time-series telemetry stores, and intermediate caching layers that require significant fast local scratch disk capacity alongside stable memory density.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.large is a storage-optimized instance engineered for storage-dense workloads requiring substantial fast local disk capacity. Powered by a 2.5 GHz arm64 AWS Graviton processor with two dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores and no hyperthreading, the instance provides 12.0 GB of RAM, a 32 MB L3 cache, and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps. Notably, the hardware profile bundles 1,875 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without GPU acceleration. Benchmark performance reflects its two-core profile, displaying modest multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth alongside steady single-core execution and 2.41 million Redis operations per second. With an advantageous ratio of NVMe disk capacity to compute, the is4gen.large offers efficient resource density for distributed storage nodes, localized database deployments, time-series data indexing, and high-capacity intermediate caching layers that do not demand extensive CPU overhead.
